content5.ptxt: The engine control computer monitors the purification condition of the catalyst using the 2 sensors installed upstream and downstream of the three-way catalytic converter. The air fuel ratio sensor sends a signal for the air-fuel ratio upstream of the catalyst to the engine control computer. The oxygen sensor sends a signal for the oxygen concentration downstream of the catalyst to the engine control computer. Based on the output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor, the engine control computer calculates the oxygen storage capacity (hereafter OSC) and detects catalyst deterioration.

While the vehicle is being driven after the engine has warmed up, the engine control computer performs active air-fuel ratio control for approximately 30 seconds or more. At this time, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. If the lean/rich cycle of the oxygen sensor is long at this point, the OSC is judged to be large.
If the OSC value is equal to or less than the judgment value, the engine control computer determines that the catalyst has deteriorated and illuminates the check engine warning light.

entry.ptxt: When all of the following conditions are met

topic.title: Confirmation Driving
topic.ptxt: By performing confirmation driving, it is possible to check whether the DTC is reproduced.

item.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) display screen, clear the DTCs. (see )
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (Engine coolant temperature 75°C or higher) (A)
Drive the vehicle at 60 to 100 km/h for 5 minutes or more. (B)
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the DTC judgment result. (see )

atten2.ptxt: When performing this driving test, be sure to obey speed limits and other traffic laws.

atten4.ptxt: If the DTC judgment result is pending or incomplete, drive the vehicle again at 60 to 100 km/h for 5 minutes or more (C), then check the DTC judgment result. If it is still pending or incomplete, drive the vehicle again at 75 to 100 km/h for 10 minutes or more (D), then check the DTC judgment result.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON. (C)
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher) (D)
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 to 3000 r/min for approximately 3 minutes. (E)
Then maintain the engine speed at 3000 r/min for 2 seconds, followed by 2000 r/min for 2 seconds. (F)
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the output voltages of [ECU Data Monitor] - [O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2] and [A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1].
If the output voltage of the air fuel ratio sensor or oxygen sensor does not fluctuate or has noise, the sensor may be malfunctioning.
If the output voltages of both sensors remain lean or rich, the air-fuel ratio may be extremely lean or rich.
When the catalyst deteriorates, the output voltage of the oxygen sensor changes greatly even under normal driving conditions.

atten4.ptxt: The malfunctioning area can be identified by performing the [Injection Volume] active test. This active test can decrease the fuel injection volume by -12.5% or increase it by +24.8%.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher)
While depressing the accelerator pedal, keep the engine speed at 2500 r/min for approximately 3 minutes to warm up each sensor.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select [Active Test] - [Fuel Injection Volume], and select [ECU Data Monitor] - [A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1] and [O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2].

With the engine idling, read the output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor when the fuel injection volume is increased and decreased using the Active Test [Fuel Injection Volume].

specitem.ptxt: The output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor change according to the increase and decrease in fuel injection volume.

atten3.ptxt: The sensors will cool down, so measure the voltage immediately after warming up the sensors.

item.ptxt: If the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage remains at approximately 3.3 V in any of the conditions, including the above condition (see the malfunction case in the illustration), the air fuel ratio sensor may have an open circuit. (This also occurs when the air fuel ratio sensor heater circuit is open.)
If the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage remains at approximately 3.8 V or more, or 2.8 V or less in any of the conditions, the air fuel ratio sensor may have a short circuit.
The engine control computer stops fuel injection during engine deceleration (fuel cut). This causes a lean condition and results in a momentary increase in the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage.

During fuel enrichment, the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage may be below 2.8 V. For the vehicle, this corresponds to sudden acceleration with the accelerator pedal fully depressed, such as when overtaking. The air fuel ratio sensor is functioning normally.

The air fuel ratio sensor is a current output element. Therefore, the current is converted into voltage inside the engine control computer. Measuring the voltage at the air fuel ratio sensor connector or engine control computer connector will show a constant voltage result.
